newsitem.title: UK: UK bookmakers cut odds on Labour election victory.
newsitem.headline: UK bookmakers cut odds on Labour election victory.

text.p: British bookmakers Ladbrokes said they were forced to cut the odds on an opposition Labour election victory twice on Monday as a wave of bets on Tony Blair's party came flooding in.
A growing conviction that Prime Minister John Major will be defeated in the May 1 poll was also evident from a significant increase in bets on who will succeed him as Conservative Party leader.
"This is the busiest day of election betting so far," Ladbrokes election betting manager Simon Clare said in a statement.

"We took well over 100,000 pounds ($164,000) this morning on Labour winning the election and cut the odds to 1-7, but the bets still came flooding in, and we were forced to shorten the odds even further to 1-8 this afternoon."
Ladbroke lengthened the odds of a Conservative victory to 9-2 from 7-2. "This is the longest price they have been since before the 1992 general election."

In the betting for who will be the next Conservative leader, Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, Home Secretary Michael Howard and Welsh Secretary William Hague are joint favourites at 3-1, Ladbrokes said.
But right-wing Eurosceptic John Redwood, who unsuccessfully challenged Major for the leadership in 1995 was attracting "large bets", the company added.
